english.title: Have a corrosive substance in a public place
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without good reason or lawful authority, had a corrosive substance, namely **(..SPECIFY CORROSIVE SUBSTANCE..), with you in a public place, namely **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 6(1) and (7) of the Offensive Weapons Act 2019.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
without good reason or lawful authority
had with them
a corrosive substance
in a public place

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) 'Corrosive substance' means a substance which is capable of burning human skin by corrosion as defined in section 6(9).
(ii) 'Public place' includes any place to which, at the time in question, the public have or are permitted access, whether on payment or otherwise as defined in section 6(9).
(iii) Defence under section 6(3) for use of work would be included within good reason or lawful authority.
(iv) Stop and search powers are available under section 1 of PACE.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 4 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Notes
In relation to an offence committed before section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 comes into force, the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.
